transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because things at work kind of swung really hard. I was suddenly taking on nonstop plant redesign projects, calling suppliers after hours, rewriting the shift plan myself—just pushing a lot of things forward at once. And then I hit this point where I couldn’t keep up with all the plans I’d started. It got pretty overwhelming.
During that time, did you feel unusually euphoric or on top of the world?

Yeah… at the start I felt almost electrically upbeat, like I was on a roll and everything made sense. Not exactly “on top of the world,” but close. And then I got weirdly irritable—like if anyone questioned my ideas, it felt like they were just slowing down something that was obvious and important.
During that period, did you need much less sleep than usual and still feel energetic?

Yeah. I was only sleeping maybe two or three hours a night, but I’d still go into the plant feeling sharp and kind of charged. It honestly felt like sleep was optional, like it was just slowing me down.
During that high-energy period, did you have any beliefs that other people said were unrealistic or not true?

Yeah. I thought I could fix the whole production workflow myself, faster than the consulting team we’d brought in. At the time it didn’t feel unrealistic at all—I was completely sure I had it figured out, and when people raised concerns, I just brushed them off because failure honestly didn’t seem possible.
Did this high-energy period ever lead to you being hospitalized?
No, I wasn’t hospitalized for it. It got serious, but it didn’t get to the point where I was admitted anywhere.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?
Yes. It’s been more than two weeks—closer to about three months now. I’ve felt depressed most of the day nearly every day, and the move and the plant assignment have made it a lot harder to handle.
